title: Improved computational method to generate properly equilibrated atomistic microstructures
author: Gupta, Rajaram, et al.
materials: To expedite the equilibration process, it is generally carried out at higher temperatures (400–600 K) in previous atomistic studies [7,14,15]. In these studies, the annealing durations were very small (10–50 ps). Consequentially, no significant grain growth was reported. However, imposing higher temperatures during thermal equilibration could lead to significant grain growth, especially in NC materials which have larger fraction of higher energy interfacial structures. It results in a larger thermodynamic driving force for grain growth in NC systems to minimize the total energy by reducing interfacial area. For instance, the average grain size of the NC Ni structure, employed in this study, grew from 6 nm to 7.3 nm and 10.5 nm at annealing temperatures of 800 K and 1000 K, respectively, only after 1 ns. One way to prevent grain growth might be subjecting only the GB and the surrounding edge atoms to high temperature equilibration and fixing the remaining grain center atoms. Moreover, as shown earlier, it is only the GB atoms that contributed the most towards the decrease in the system's potential energy during regular thermal equilibration simulation. Thus, we propose a two-step equilibration method.

steps.title: Generate initial NC Ni structure
steps.instruction: Create a nanocrystalline Ni model using the phase‑field method (Gruber et al.). Set the simulation box to 18 nm × 18 nm × 18 nm with periodic boundaries in all directions. The structure should contain ~40 grains, an average grain size of 6 nm, and about 500 000 atoms. Use LAMMPS with the Embedded‑Atom Model (EAM) potential for Ni (reference [20]) and visualize with OVITO. Determine grain size and grain count with the method of [22].

steps.title: Run regular 300 K equilibration
steps.instruction: Equilibrate the entire system in LAMMPS using an NPT ensemble at 300 K, maintaining zero normal pressure on all periodic faces. Use a 1 fs timestep. Continue the simulation until the potential energy stabilises (moving‑average plateau and standard deviation < 0.5 eV over the last 1 ns), which occurs at ≈ 21 ns (≈ 21 million steps).

steps.title: Perform tensile test on equilibrated structure
steps.instruction: Apply uniaxial tension at 300 K with a constant engineering strain rate of 1 × 10⁸ s⁻¹ along one axis while keeping zero normal pressure on the transverse axes (NPT ensemble). Load to a total strain of 12 %. Record the global pressure tensor every 1000 steps and average over the preceding 100 steps to obtain stress. Compute elastic stiffness from the stress‑strain slope below 1 % strain and yield strength using the 0.2 % offset method. Save atomic configurations (positions and velocities) every 0.2 % strain up to 3 % strain for possible restart, then unload at the same strain rate to zero stress and calculate residual strain.

steps.title: Identify atom groups for two‑step equilibration
steps.instruction: Classify atoms into three groups: (i) Grain‑center atoms – FCC‑structured atoms whose six‑nearest‑neighbour shells (≈ 6.1 Å) are all FCC (distinguishes grains with misorientation ≥ 8.5°). (ii) Grain‑edge atoms – FCC atoms that do not meet the full‑neighbor criterion. (iii) GB atoms – non‑FCC atoms in disordered regions. Fix the positions of all grain‑center atoms for the first equilibration step.

steps.title: High‑temperature NVT equilibration of GB/edge atoms
steps.instruction: Run a canonical (NVT) simulation with the system volume fixed. First equilibrate the mobile GB and edge atoms at 300 K for 0.1 ns. Then heat them to a chosen high temperature (Thigh, typically 400–600 K) and hold for a chosen duration (thigh, e.g., 10–50 ps). Finally cool the mobile atoms back to 300 K while the grain‑center atoms remain fixed.

steps.title: Final NPT equilibration of whole system
steps.instruction: Release the constraints on grain‑center atoms and equilibrate the entire system at 300 K in an NPT ensemble with zero normal pressure in all directions. Use a 1 fs timestep and run until the same convergence criteria as the regular method (potential‑energy moving‑average plateau, standard deviation < 0.5 eV over the last 1 ns).

steps.title: Mechanical testing of two‑step equilibrated structure
steps.instruction: Repeat the tensile‑loading protocol described in step 3 on the structure obtained after the two‑step equilibration, using the same strain rate, temperature, and analysis procedures.
